answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive in a delayed way. Each newcomer posts a jade collateral bond that stays locked for several epochs while peers watch its behavior. Only after that trial reaches its zenith—no clustered keys, no copy-paste timing, no sudden swarm of aliases—does the agent gain voting weight. A public sable ledger then records every slashed cluster, automatically raising the next bond so cloning identities costs more than honest work.
